Multistate model for one treatment group

Source: R/ms_model.R
ms_model.Rd

Defines the four-state model of one group: progression-free and alive (state 1), progressed without switch (state 2), switched (state 3) and dead (state 4). Progression-free survival (PFS) is the time to leave state 1 and overall survival (OS) is the time to enter state 4.

Usage

ms_model(
  time = 0,
  prog = 0,
  death,
  death_prog = NULL,
  switch_prob = 0,
  switch_rate = 0,
  death_switch = NULL,
  dropout = 0,
  time_post = 0,
  clock = c("reset", "forward")
)

Arguments

time

Interval start times for the pre-progression intensities and the dropout hazard. Must start at 0 and be strictly increasing.

prog

Progression hazard in each interval (length 1 or length(time)).

death

Hazard of death before progression in each interval.

death_prog

Hazard of death after progression without switch, in each interval of time_post. Required when prog is positive in some interval.

switch_prob

Probability of switching immediately at progression, in each interval of time.

switch_rate

Hazard of switching after progression, in each interval of time_post.

death_switch

Hazard of death after a switch, in each interval of time_post. Defaults to death_prog, that is, switching has no effect on survival.

dropout

Dropout hazard in each interval of time.

time_post

Interval start times for the post-progression intensities. Must start at 0 and be strictly increasing.

clock

Clock of the post-progression intensities: "reset" (time since progression) or "forward" (time since randomization).

Value

An object of class ms_model: a list with the intensity vectors expanded to the lengths of time and time_post, and clock.

Details

Before progression, the intensities are piecewise constant in the time since randomization, with intervals starting at time: progression (prog), death before progression (death), and the probability switch_prob of switching immediately at progression (evaluated at the time of progression). After progression without switch, the patient dies with intensity death_prog or switches with intensity switch_rate; after a switch, the patient dies with intensity death_switch. The post-progression intensities are piecewise constant with intervals starting at time_post.

With clock = "reset" (default) the post-progression intensities are functions of the time since progression (a semi-Markov model). With clock = "forward" they are functions of the time since randomization (a Markov model). The two clocks give the same model when the post-progression intensities are constant.

Dropout is piecewise exponential with intervals starting at time, independent of the event process, and censors both endpoints.

A model without progression (prog = 0) is a piecewise exponential model for a single endpoint with hazard death. With death_prog = death, switch_prob = 0 and switch_rate = 0, the model is that of Fleischer et al. (2009); see ms_fleischer.

References

Fleischer F, Gaschler-Markefski B, Bluhmki E (2009). A statistical model for the dependence between progression-free survival and overall survival. Statistics in Medicine 28:2669-2686.

See also

ms_fleischer, ms_scenario, ms_surv, ms_prob

Examples

# Single endpoint: exponential survival with a median of 12 months
ms_model(death = log(2) / 12)
#> Four-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog      death switch_prob dropout
#>     0    0 0.05776227           0       0

# Progression, with 30 percent of the patients switching at progression
ms_model(time = c(0, 6), prog = c(0.10, 0.08), death = 0.01,
         death_prog = 0.05, switch_prob = 0.3, death_switch = 0.03)
#> Four-state model for one group (clock after progression: "reset")
#> Before progression (time since randomization):
#>  time prog death switch_prob dropout
#>     0 0.10  0.01         0.3       0
#>     6 0.08  0.01         0.3       0
#> After progression (time since progression):
#>  time_post death_prog switch_rate death_switch
#>          0       0.05           0         0.03
